idea: Generate perfect and imperfect squared rectangles via Brooks–Smith–Stone–Tutte electrical networks. Enumerate small planar graphs (up to about n+3 edges), solve Kirchhoff's equations exactly with Fractions to get square dissections of a square with exactly n tiles, and take the best sum. Near-square rectangle dissections are also kept, scaled into the unit square with the leftover strip filled by zero-size or small squares.
